content:
emma: Heads up — paging failed after the 12:10 deploy, looks like incidentbot didn't forward to the oncall group.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: release 2026.03.17-7 deployed to prod-1 at 12:10 UTC
emma: I can see incident-bot returned 429 from the notify-proxy and then stopped trying. stack shows: `notify-proxy -> pagerbridge -> pagerflow`
rick: I didn't receive any pages. alejandro, did you get anything?
alejandro: nothing from incidentbot, I only saw a manual SMS from emma.
lina: quick paste from notify-proxy logs (12:11 — 12:17):
```
2026-03-17T12:11:05Z notify-proxy ERROR outbound request to pagerbridge failed status=429 body="rate limit"
2026-03-17T12:11:05Z incident-bot WARN webhook retry scheduled retry=1
2026-03-17T12:11:10Z notify-proxy ERROR outbound request to pagerbridge failed status=429 body="rate limit"
2026-03-17T12:12:02Z incident-bot INFO giving up after retries
```

marta: PagerBridge metrics show an outbound spike at 12:11 — 2k/min then a 429 surge.
emma: any config changes in the deploy? we toggled a header name for webhook auth.
lina: yes — header renamed from X-Notify-Sig to X-Notify-Signature in the client. pagerbridge treats unknown header as unauthenticated which triggers a fallback path hitting a different rate-limited endpoint.
rick: Ok. Immediate mitigation: can we route incidentbot -> fallback-notify direct or bump pagerbridge limit?
alexander: (alejandro) I'm on it. temporarily bumped pagerbridge tenant limit to 3000/min and restarting notify-proxy.
ops-bot: restart notify-proxy-prod-1: accepted
ops-bot: restart notify-proxy-prod-1: success
incident-bot: incident-bot: created I-2026-123 and attempted page to @platform-oncall — previous attempts failed; new attempt sent
emma: manual pages sent to SRE leads while we fix. customers may have seen errors.
alejandro: initial impact: ~5% requests experienced elevated errors (502/503) for tenants tenant-a and tenant-c between 12:11–12:16. approx 12 active users affected total.
marta: exported error-rate by tenant: https://internal/reports/err/1769012345 (shared)
lina: root-cause hypothesis: header rename caused notify-proxy to route to the fallback auth path which hit a stricter rate limiter — retry storm from the client made it worse.
emma: mitigation steps summary: 1) bump rate limits 2) restart notify-proxy 3) revert header change in client and redeploy 4) temporarily disable automated paging to avoid noisy failures
ops-bot: toggle incidentbot-automatic-paging=false: success
alejandro: I've kicked a revert for the header change; build queued. also adding a short-term circuit in client to stop retrying on 429.
rick: after revert and restart, confirm paging path healthy and re-enable auto paging.
ops-bot: healthcheck notify-proxy-prod-1: OK (latency nominal)
incident-bot: page to @platform-oncall succeeded at 12:22 UTC
emma: good. customer impact low but visible. We'll draft a customer note and open a retro.
rick: postmortem owners: alejandro + emma. action items: add integration test for header auth, add rate-limit telemetry alert, document runbook for disabling automated paging.
emma: thanks everyone — will open the retro thread and the follow-up epic. :thumbsup:
